why: Confirm the perception-reaction time available to the colliding drivers matches the 10.43 s sight distance finding.
command: cd /workspace/job && mkdir -p repo out && cp -r /workspace/repo/checks /workspace/repo/web repo/ && npm i --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error three@0.186.1 >/dev/null && node run_task.mjs --repo /workspace/job/repo --world /workspace/job/world.js --task-file /workspace/job/task.json --out /workspace/job/out/result.json

agentReply.interpretation: Both drivers had an unobstructed line of sight for 10.43 seconds prior to impact, providing sufficient perception-reaction time.

prt.detail: The driver of Vehicle A had a continuous line of sight to Vehicle T Semitrailer for 10.43 s before impact (t=0.00–10.43 s), from the start of the reconstructed timeline, so this is a lower bound. Typical perception-reaction time is 1.5 s (range 1–2.5 s). Time available is more than the 2.5 s upper bound, so there was time to perceive and begin reacting. Vehicle T Semitrailer came within 3 m of the centerline of this driver's remaining path 2.38 s before impact. Kinematic estimate from the reconstructed geometry; it does not account for attention, conspicuity, glare or expectation.
